thread:
alex: Quick sync — onboarding nova-70b checkpoint. Finalizing conversion+packaging. I have a few open Qs: weights location, safetensors conversion flags, TP layout expectations, and tokenizer quirks. Can folks drop the minimal steps they use?

maria: weights are in s3://redwood-models/nova70b/v1/ — files: shard_00.safetensors .. shard_07.safetensors, plus model_index.json (sha256 in manifest).

ken: TP layout note: this model was exported with tensor-parallel=8 using interleaved split (we split along dim=0 for linear weights). Serving expects contiguous TP shards (shard_map in model_index maps original slices). If you see naming like "transformer.wi.weight.split0" that's interleaved. Our converter will reorder if you pass --tp-src interleaved --tp-tgt contiguous.

nico: tokenizer quirk: it was trained with sentencepiece. The vocab has <unk> id=0 and BOS not used. When we serve with our GPT-ish tokenizer wrapper, set "add_bos": false and "bos_token": null, otherwise generation prepends extra token. Also watch for normalization differences (NFKC vs none).

eva: conversion command I used locally (works for safetensors):
```bash
safetensors-convert \ 
  --input-dir s3://redwood-models/nova70b/v1/ \ 
  --output ./packaged/nova70b_v1/ \ 
  --dtype fp16 \ 
  --tp-src interleaved --tp-tgt contiguous \ 
  --shard-size 200MB \ 
  --manifest-out packaged/manifest.json
```
Note: add `--keep-keys order` if you need deterministic key ordering for checksum.

alex: thanks. On dtype: fp16 or bf16? any gotchas?

ken: prefer fp16 for this release (NVIDIA A100 gen2 perf tested). bf16 is fine but some ops in our kernel path fallback differently — we saw slightly higher latency on bf16 for long context. Also check for `layernorm` params cast back to fp32 in serving config.

nico: also, when converting, ensure KV cache tensor ordering matches our runtime: cache layout expects [num_layers, 2, batch, head, seq, head_dim]. If the exporter wrote [batch, num_layers, ...] you'll get garbage. Quick python sanity:
```python
import torch
t = torch.load('packaged/nova70b_v1/kv_cache_sample.pt')
assert t.shape[0] == num_layers, 'kv cache first axis != num_layers'
```
If that fails, run `kv-reorder --from exporter --to runtime` (we have helper in tools/).

maria: manifest.json includes shard_map and tp_world_size. I pushed a small script to validate layout: `scripts/validate_shards.py packaged/manifest.json` — it checks sizes, checksums, key sets. Run it before upload.

eva: add: 8) run `model-lint --allowed-extra-keys` to ensure no unexpected param names; 9) run small-batch perf with batch sizes [1,4,8] to ensure no perf cliffs.
